A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DFloat11 and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Inspection covers Appendices A–D in v1 and A–K in v2, allowing relocated material to be distinguished from substantive changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression measurements, accuracy and perplexity evaluations, GPU inference benchmarks, and decompression analyses in Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original compression and inference measurements, language benchmarks, diffusion-model memory and timing results, and paired generated images in Tables 1–3 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: v1's four-LUT decoder with frequency adjustments for ambiguous prefixes becomes a hierarchy of 4–8 pointer-linked LUTs in v2 Section 2.3.1. Algorithm 1 adds an SRAM output buffer and coalesced HBM writes. Compression also expands from linear projection weights to include token embeddings, substantially revising the procedure and compressed components.

E1.justification: v2 extends the LLM evaluation to text-to-image diffusion transformers, including FLUX.1 and Stable Diffusion 3.5, with compression, memory, timing, and generated-image evidence. The language benchmarks MMLU, TruthfulQA, WikiText, and C4, plus the Math/GPQA quantization comparison, remain represented.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain BF16 counterparts, CPU-to-GPU weight transfer, and NVIDIA nvCOMP ANS. The quantization table retains BF16 and INT8. Diffusion experiments extend the BF16 comparison to the added task; altered GPU allocations change protocols rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix C compares one-GPU DF11 against two-GPU BF16; v2 Appendix G instead uses matched A100 configurations with Flash Attention enabled for both. Model and batch configurations also change, including Qwen2.5 being replaced by Qwen3 in offloading tests and revised latency-breakdown batch sizes. New diffusion evaluations measure 1024×1024 image generation on one A5000.

E4.justification: The retained latency-breakdown and matrix-size analyses are revised, including an additional token-embedding decompression component. Appendix J adds five paired image-output cases. Conversely, v1's explicit verification of bit-level weight equivalence across every model in its compression table is no longer reported.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty values for diffusion generation times in Table 3 and reports five runs for that experiment, although the meaning of the ± statistic is unspecified. Existing five-run decoding averages, ten-run latency breakdowns, and uncertainty reporting for retained language accuracy results remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerous results change: Llama 3.1 8B's compressed size goes from 11.24 to 10.90 GB with broader compression scope, and DF11 throughput for the reported A100/4096×65536 matrix setting rises from 189.1 to 262.1 GB/s. v2 adds diffusion and compression-time results and replaces the appendix GPU results. Qwen2.5 accuracy rows disappear, while retained Llama benchmark scores and INT8 errors are identical.

T1.justification: The BF16 value formula, Shannon entropy definition, and prefix-free Huffman background are retained. Appendix I expands algorithmic explanation through worked lookup-table examples; it introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion explicitly expand the paper's empirical scope from LLMs to LLMs and diffusion models. Headline offloading speedups change from 1.9–38.8× to 2.3–46.2×, and generation-length multipliers also change under revised evaluations. The central approximately 30% lossless compression and single-node Llama 405B claims remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix K explicitly limits applicability to BF16 weights and GPU evaluation and discusses consequences for latency-sensitive, small-batch applications. The introduction adds behavioral correctness flips and reliability concerns to the motivation for preserving outputs. The interpretation that larger batches amortize decompression overhead is retained.

D1.justification: v2 identifies Blelloch's prefix-scan algorithm and documents compression times measured using one CPU thread in Appendix F. It omits v1's explicit setting of 256 threads per block. The CUDA/C++, Transformers/Accelerate implementation information and code repository address remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds context on diffusion quantization, behavioral flips, safety and reliability, and SF4, and explicitly attributes hierarchical LUT decomposition to the already-cited Yamamoto work. The central positioning relative to Deep Compression, ZipNN, NeuZip, and Huff-LLM remains, with extended discussion relocated to Appendix B.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial method and experiment prose are rewritten and condensed. The motivation discussion moves to Appendix A, extended related work moves to Appendix B, and detailed decoding explanations are added in Appendix I. Numerous numbered experimental subsections become paragraph headings, substantially changing the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds hierarchical-decoding and thread-offset diagrams, worked LUT figures, a paired image grid, and diffusion and compression-time tables. It removes v1's hardware-feasibility table, reorganizes the compression table and performance panels, and relocates Algorithm 1 to the appendix. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 makes deployment tradeoffs easier to assess through matched-GPU comparisons, compression-time measurements, and explicit limitations. Expanded decoder explanations and diffusion validation strengthen clarity and empirical support. These benefits are tempered by removing Qwen2.5 accuracy results, the explicit all-model bit-level verification, and the threads-per-block setting, yielding a limited net improvement.
